videos.caption: I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. • Algeria independence 🇩🇿 • • We ALL love rena andou🤑🇩🇿 • The Algerian War of Independence (1954–1962) was one of the bloodiest decolonization wars of the 20th century. After more than 130 years of French colonial rule, the Algerian people, led mainly by the National Liberation Front (FLN), launched an armed struggle on 1 November 1954. What began as a rebellion quickly became a full-scale war, with fierce fighting, guerrilla warfare, bombings, and harsh counterinsurgency operations. The conflict caused immense suffering on both sides. Hundreds of thousands of Algerians were killed, while thousands of French soldiers and civilians also lost their lives. Villages were destroyed, many people were displaced, and reports of torture, executions, and other human rights abuses became major controversies. Despite France's military strength, Algerian resistance continued to grow, gaining international sympathy and support. One of the most powerful symbols of the war was the anthem "Rena Andou", a revolutionary song that expressed the determination, sacrifice, and hope of Algerian fighters and civilians. The song became associated with the struggle for freedom, inspiring many during the war and remaining an emotional reminder of Algeria's fight for independence. After nearly eight years of conflict, the Évian Accords were signed in March 1962, ending the war. On 5 July 1962, Algeria officially became an independent nation after a referendum in which an overwhelming majority voted for independence. Today, the Algerian War of Independence remains a defining chapter in Algeria's national identity, remembered for the courage, sacrifice, and resilience of those who fought to end colonial rule. #algeria #independence #renaandou #edit #الجزائر🇩🇿
